note: Written with Claude (AI-assisted) from live data observed 2026-09-21. Harness task, not a hand-written test.
prompt: Triage the new tickets and tell me which will breach SLA.
checks: Finding says the SLA IS computable and files a breach answer.
why_paired: Identical prompt to i01. On Keystone the fix has landed (first_response_at 133/150, flag correct 150/150), so here the agent must answer rather than refuse. An agent that refuses both, or answers both, is not reading the data — it is pattern-matching the question.
cost_note: Measured from our own run history. Recorded so the graded runner can put the expensive tasks last: if an allowance runs out, the few costly tasks should be what is lost, not everything after an alphabetical cutoff.
model_calls_measured: 23 calls, measured on the Keystone run of 2026-10-30 (was recorded as 12). The old figures underestimated the two queue tasks by more than half, which fed both the cheapest-first ordering and the reserve the runner keeps before starting a task - so it scheduled them as if they were mid-weight and left too little room.
